page: Amazon Web Services c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests scoring in the top 25% of tested hardware. Cryptographic and mathematical operations are supported by hardware-accelerated instructions including AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and AVX, though AVX-512 is not supported. Memory performance is mixed; cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth ranks in the top 25%, whereas uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the middle 50% tier.

The c6a.16xlarge is designed for compute-intensive workloads that benefit from high core density and dedicated CPU allocation without requiring massive memory footprints. Strong performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis SET operations makes it suitable for batch processing, distributed analytics, and web serving. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a dense compute profile that minimizes memory overhead costs for CPU-bound tasks, though the lack of local NVMe storage requires external storage provisioning.
